elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: New 4.10(ii): "the operation and maintenance duties it performs under Paragraph 10 will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner."

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: New 4.10(i): "its Segment T, including any software incorporated in it, will conform in all material respects to the facilities, functions and documentation specified for it in Annex 8".

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Inserted period is "ninety (90) days following the RFS Date", not twelve months; drafter acknowledges the 12-month period was not sought.
Services (O&M duties) warranty runs only "thirty (30) days following performance".

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "the responsible Terminal Party shall promptly repair or replace the non-conforming Segment T or re-perform the non-conforming duties".
"or, if it does not do so within a reasonable period, refund the amounts paid by the Parties in respect of the non-conforming Segment T or duties" — refund is expressly available as a remedy.

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty anywhere in the inserted 4.10 or elsewhere; drafter expressly reserved this as a further ask.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code warranty is included in the rendered language.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: 4.10(i) expressly warrants software ("including any software incorporated in it") conforms in all material respects to the Annex 8 documentation for 90 days — an express software-to-documentation warranty, not a mere manual-conformance for outputs.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: 4.10(ii) warrants the Paragraph 10 operation and maintenance duties for "thirty (30) days following performance" to a professional and workmanlike standard.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "promptly repair or replace the non-conforming Segment T or re-perform the non-conforming duties".

Refund of "the amounts paid by the Parties in respect of the non-conforming Segment T or duties" is available if repair/replacement/re-performance is not completed in a reasonable period — a tiered but real refund remedy.

reasons: Baseline classification is correct: the only warranty language is the Subparagraph 4.9 disclaimer (PG makes no representations or warranties; "nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as such a warranty or guarantee"), with no express performance warranty, period or remedy running to us — walk-away territory, so a redline (insertion) is warranted.

Fallback checklist is complete: 90-day software/Segment T conformance to Annex 8 documentation, 30-day professional-and-workmanlike warranty for the O&M duties, and repair/replace/re-perform plus refund remedies are all in operative text.

Preferred level is not reached (90 days rather than 12 months for software, 30 days rather than 90 for services, and no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranties); that is an acceptable fallback landing and correctly disclosed in the comment as a further ask.

Minimality holds: a single concise new subparagraph for a missing clause, the Customer-favourable PG disclaimer in 4.9 is left untouched, no survival tail, no expense or damages boilerplate, and the professional-and-workmanlike standard is the substantive standard the services element requires rather than an extra.

Intent preserved: the new warranty is scoped to Segment T and Paragraph 10 O&M duties, which are distinct from the Supply Contract, Wet Segment and integration matters disclaimed in 4.9, so no retained sentence contradicts it; direction is correct because the warranty binds Terminal Parties (Teleglobe is not one) and runs to the other Parties, including us.

Repair before drafting goes out: confirm "RFS Date" is a defined term in the Agreement — the cited text uses only "RFPA Date as specified in the Supply Contract"; if RFS Date is undefined, re-anchor the 90-day period to the RFPA Date or another defined milestone so the trigger is not open-ended.

Also verify the cross-references "Annex 8" (facilities, functions and documentation for Segment T) and "Paragraph 10" (operation and maintenance duties) and confirm the inserted subparagraph number 4.10 is unused — the rationale refers to the disclaimer as spanning "4.9-4.10", so renumber to avoid a duplicate-number/dangling reference.
